**v1.10.1: with two Wizard101 windows open, Cheat Engine's speedhack now speeds up the one the bot walks - never the other account's.**
- **What was wrong.** With the speedhack set up by Setup.exe, Cheat Engine's script (CheatEngine\wiz-maxxing.lua) moved Cheat Engine to the newest Wizard101 every 2 s. So a second account started while the bot walked took the bot's speed keys: the bot's window was left sped up, out of reach of the 1x key (Cheat Engine speeds up only the game it has open, and one it leaves keeps its speed), and the next walk sped up the other account. In dual mode (Alt+D) the newest window was sped up whichever one the bot walked.
- **What happens now.** The walking key speeds up the Wizard101 window in front - the one the bot walks (it presses that key only with a game window in front). When Cheat Engine has the other one, the script sets that one back to 1x first, while Cheat Engine is still on it, then moves Cheat Engine to the window in front and speeds it up. With no game window in front, the walking key speeds up only the window it sped up last. The 1x key sets the window Cheat Engine has back to 1x, and only when it's sped up: it never switches the speedhack on, so a battle round while Cheat Engine is on the other account no longer puts Cheat Engine's speedhack into that game. Every 2 s the script still attaches Cheat Engine to Wizard101 when it has none - the window in front, else the newest - or when that game has exited; it no longer moves off a game that's running, and never sets a speed. So in dual mode the speed follows the walked window, with one move each time the bot switches windows, and another account you play by hand is never sped up.
- **Unchanged:** one game window plays as before; the keys, the speed and their Settings; a process you opened in Cheat Engine yourself is never touched (the keys no longer speed it up either); nothing comes up by itself (a step that fails still says so once, in a box starting "Wiz-Maxxing (autorun\wiz-maxxing.lua)"). With the script there, Cheat Engine follows the bot: a table of your own open in Cheat Engine is switched off when it moves (Cheat Engine does that on every move).
- **To get it, run Setup.exe once, tick Cheat Engine speedhack, Install, restart Cheat Engine.** The updater brings the bot's copy of the script, but Cheat Engine keeps the one Setup put in its autorun folder, and runs it only when it starts. Until then the bot says so once a run, in debug.log only (no box): "Speedhack: on - Cheat Engine's Wiz-Maxxing script is older - run Setup.exe, tick Cheat Engine speedhack, Install, then restart Cheat Engine".
- **Still possible:** a window left sped up before this version (or by Cheat Engine crashing while it was fast) stays so till that game restarts: the 1x key acts only on a speed this Cheat Engine set itself (one started again, or just moved to that window, reads 1x), and on 7.6 and later a new speed sits on top of the old one; Cheat Engine 7.6 and later (what Setup installs) put their speedhack into a window again each time Cheat Engine comes back to it, which an hour of dual mode has to show is fine; Cheat Engine's own automatic attach with "Even autoattach when another process has already been selected" ticked moves it without the 1x first - leave that off; with two game windows the bot's auto-reconnect and its turn check can still pick the other window, as before.
- **Not tried in the game yet.** The script and the bot's check were only read, and the script run against a model of Cheat Engine, not against the game (no Cheat Engine or Windows where they were made). AutoFarmer\LIVE_CHECKS.txt steps 5.5a-5.5i say what to look for and what to send, after 5.3 and 5.4 (the speedhack with one game window, not tried in the game yet either).
- **Updating:** the updater offers this to every install, including ones set up from the v0.7.0 or v0.7.1 zips. Your settings, learned cards and routes are kept. A copy run from the code: git pull.
